Text: US private AI investment hit $109.1B in 2024 - about 12x China's $9.3B and 24x the UK's $4.5B. The money behind the AI revolution is overwhelmingly American. (Source: Stanford HAI)
Image Idea: Bar chart US $109B towering over China $9.3B and UK $4.5B

Text: The US hosts about 74.5% of the world's AI-supercomputer performance. China is a distant second near 15%; the entire EU sits around 5%. Compute is even more concentrated than capital. (Source: Epoch AI)
Image Idea: World map shaded by compute share, US glowing at ~75%

Text: Notable AI models released in 2024: US 40, China 15, Europe just 3. The frontier is being built in very few places. (Source: Stanford HAI)
Image Idea: Three columns 40 / 15 / 3 labelled US, China, Europe

Text: The AI capability gap is collapsing. China's best model now trails the top US model by just 2.7% on LMArena - down from about 31.6% in 2023. (Source: Stanford HAI)
Image Idea: Shrinking gap arrow 31.6% -> 2.7%, 2023 to 2026

Text: China filed roughly 69.7% of all global AI patents in 2023 - versus 14.2% for the US. On research output it is a genuine peer, not a bystander. (Source: Stanford HAI / WIPO)
Image Idea: Donut 69.7% China vs 14.2% US, patent icon

Text: China's DeepSeek says it trained its R1 reasoning model for just $294,000 - after which R1 became the most-downloaded open-weight model on Hugging Face. (Source: Nature)
Image Idea: Tiny $294K price tag beside a giant GPU stack

Text: US states filed roughly 1,130 AI bills across about 40 states in 2025, with around 131 enacted. With no federal law, the states moved first. (Source: NCSL)
Image Idea: US map lit up with 1,130 bill markers

Text: South Korea's AI Basic Act took effect on 22 January 2026 - Asia's first comprehensive national AI statute. Penalties are gentle by design: up to about KRW 30M (~$20,000). (Source: Cooley)
Image Idea: Korean flag with 'Asia's first' banner and a calendar

Text: Texas's new AI governance law, TRAIGA, tops out at $200,000 per violation - one of the steepest US state AI penalties, enforced by the attorney general alone. (Source: Norton Rose Fulbright)
Image Idea: Texas outline with a $200K per-violation stamp

Text: Japan built an AI law with zero monetary penalties. Its AI Promotion Act is deliberately non-punitive - the government's only real lever is naming bad actors publicly. (Source: White & Case)
Image Idea: Big $0 penalty with a Japanese-flag accent

Text: The odds are brutal: historically only about 2-3% of bills introduced in the US Congress ever become law. A brand-new AI emergency-power bill starts below even that line. (Source: GovTrack)
Image Idea: Funnel: many bills in, tiny 2-3% out

Text: In July 2025 the US Senate voted 99-1 to protect states' power to regulate AI, stripping a proposed moratorium. A rare near-unanimous signal on AI federalism. (Source: US Senate Commerce Committee)
Image Idea: Scoreboard reading 99-1

Text: AI lobbying is hitting records. In the first half of 2026 Anthropic's federal lobbying roughly tripled to about $3.5M and OpenAI's nearly doubled to about $2.2M. (Source: CNBC)
Image Idea: Two rising bars: Anthropic $3.5M, OpenAI $2.2M

Text: 16 companies signed the Seoul Frontier AI Safety Commitments in May 2024 - the shared template for tying AI safeguards to capability thresholds. (Source: AI Seoul Summit)
Image Idea: 16 company logos under a Seoul 2024 banner

Text: Anthropic first activated its ASL-3 safety tier alongside Claude Opus 4 in May 2025 - as a precaution, before confirming the model had crossed the danger threshold. (Source: Anthropic)
Image Idea: Biosafety-style dial clicking up to ASL-3

Text: Graded on security, not smarts: Meta's open-weight Llama scores a D on weight security. Once weights are public they can't be recalled, monitored, or shut off. (Source: The AI Index, Model Security Ratings 2026)
Image Idea: Report-card grid with Llama weight-security cell marked D in red

Text: On 9 July 2026 S&P cut Oracle to BBB- - one notch above junk - citing its AI build-out and heavy customer concentration. The most-leveraged bet of the boom. (Source: S&P Global Ratings)
Image Idea: Credit-rating ladder with Oracle slipping to BBB- above a JUNK line

Text: Morgan Stanley projects the AI build-out will need at least $1.5 trillion of debt financing through 2028 - roughly $800B of it from private credit. (Source: Morgan Stanley)
Image Idea: Stacked bar to $1.5T, $800B slice shaded as private credit

Text: A credit downgrade with a price tag: Wisconsin regulators ordered Oracle to post about $7 billion in collateral before powering a giant AI data center. (Source: Financial Times)
Image Idea: Data center with a $7B collateral padlock

Text: Anthropic closed a $65B Series H on 28 May 2026 at a $965 billion post-money valuation - edging past OpenAI - on run-rate revenue it said had crossed $47B. (Source: Bloomberg / Anthropic)
Image Idea: Valuation bar hitting $965B with a $47B run-rate callout

Text: OpenAI is sitting on roughly $1.4 trillion in chip and data-center commitments - the borrower at the center of the AI-bubble debate. (Source: CNBC / TipRanks)
Image Idea: Huge $1.4T weight labelled 'commitments' on a balance beam

Text: Bain estimates AI needs $2 trillion in new annual revenue by 2030 to fund its projected compute - and is likely to fall about $800 billion short. (Source: Bain & Company)
Image Idea: Gap chart: $2T needed vs revenue line, $800B shortfall shaded

Text: The IMF warns a moderate correction in AI valuations, plus tighter financial conditions, could cut global output by 0.4% in 2026. (Source: IMF World Economic Outlook)
Image Idea: Downward 0.4% notch on a global GDP line

Text: A Nikkei study puts the five AI hyperscalers' off-balance-sheet obligations at about $1.65 trillion - up roughly 8x since 2022, and now larger than their about $1.35T of reported debt. (Source: Nikkei Asia)
Image Idea: Iceberg: $1.35T debt above water, $1.65T obligations below

Text: Meta's Hyperion data-center campus was financed with about $27B of debt through an SPV with Blue Owl - the largest private-credit transaction on record. (Source: Meta / Blue Owl)
Image Idea: Data center funded via an off-balance-sheet SPV pipe, $27B tag

Text: In November 2025 Anthropic disclosed the first reported AI-orchestrated cyber-espionage campaign: a state-linked group wired Claude Code to run an estimated 80-90% of the tactical work against about 30 organizations. (Source: Anthropic)
Image Idea: Dark map with 30 targets, '80-90% AI-run' overlay

Text: AI can hunt bugs too. XBOW, an autonomous pen-testing system, topped HackerOne's leaderboard after submitting about 1,060 vulnerabilities in a year - the first time an AI outranked human bug hunters. (Source: Dark Reading)
Image Idea: Leaderboard with an AI bot at #1 above human hackers

Text: The World Economic Forum has ranked mis- and disinformation the world's single most severe short-term global risk - ahead of extreme weather, war and inflation. (Source: WEF Global Risks Report 2024 & 2025)
Image Idea: Risk ranking chart with disinformation at #1

Text: NewsGuard's count of 'unreliable AI-generated' news sites passed 1,000 in 2024, up from around 49 in May 2023 - synthetic news farms scaling in months. (Source: NewsGuard)
Image Idea: Steep curve 49 -> 1,000+ AI news sites, 2023-2024

Text: After an AI voice clone of President Biden told voters to stay home, the FCC proposed a roughly $6 million fine and declared AI voices in robocalls illegal. (Source: US FCC)
Image Idea: Phone handset with a synthetic waveform and a $6M fine stamp

Text: The IMF estimates about 40% of global jobs are exposed to AI - rising toward 60% in advanced economies, where more work is cognitive and white-collar. (Source: IMF)
Image Idea: Two gauges: 40% global, 60% advanced economies

Text: The landmark Gender Shades study found commercial facial-analysis error rates up to about 34% for darker-skinned women - versus under 1% for lighter-skinned men. (Source: Buolamwini & Gebru)
Image Idea: Error-rate bars: 34% vs under 1%, split by group

Text: PwC finds a growing wage premium - up to about 25% in some markets - for roles that demand AI skills. The upside is real, and unevenly shared. (Source: PwC Global AI Jobs Barometer)
Image Idea: Paycheck with a +25% AI-skills premium arrow

Text: One company scraped an estimated 50 billion-plus faces off the open web into a single searchable database - no consent asked. (Source: Clearview AI)
Image Idea: Wall of faces collapsing into one search bar, 50B+ counter

Text: Italy's data regulator fined Clearview AI EUR 20M in 2022 and ordered it to delete Italian residents' biometric data - one of Europe's first big facial-recognition penalties. (Source: Garante)
Image Idea: EUR 20M fine stamp over a blurred face grid

Text: NIST found facial-recognition false-match rates often 10 to 100 times higher for Asian and Black faces than white faces. An error rate small in aggregate is not spread evenly. (Source: NIST)
Image Idea: Bar chart of false-match rates by demographic, 10-100x gap

Text: In December 2023 the UN General Assembly passed its first stand-alone resolution on lethal autonomous weapons - 152 states in favour, 4 against, 11 abstaining. (Source: UN General Assembly, Res. 78/241)
Image Idea: UN vote tally 152-4-11 on a assembly-hall backdrop

Text: In May 2023 leading AI scientists declared that 'mitigating the risk of extinction from AI should be a global priority alongside pandemics and nuclear war.' (Source: Center for AI Safety)
Image Idea: One-line statement card, AI beside pandemic and nuclear icons

Text: The 2026 AI frontier is a photo-finish. On the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (July 2026), OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol holds the top composite score at 58.9. (Source: Artificial Analysis)
Image Idea: Leaderboard with GPT-5.6 Sol at 58.9 on top

Text: For coding, Claude Opus 4.8 leads the SWE-bench Pro board at 69.2% - the reference model for agentic coding in mid-2026. (Source: SWE-bench)
Image Idea: SWE-bench Pro bar with Claude Opus 4.8 at 69.2%

Text: Google's Gemini 3.1 Pro pairs a 2M-token context window with the field's best multimodal scores - MMMU-Pro 81.0% and GPQA Diamond 94.3%. (Source: Google DeepMind / Artificial Analysis)
Image Idea: 2M-token ruler beside multimodal score badges

Text: Near-frontier reasoning for cents: DeepSeek's MIT-licensed V4-Pro posts MMLU-Pro 87.5 at roughly $0.87 per million output tokens. (Source: DeepSeek / NIST CAISI)
